I am 73 years old this year, and I have been farming these fields in Quzhou since I was a young man. My family has 5 mu of land — not much, but it is what we have. I only went to primary school, so I do not read those extension pamphlets. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Old Wang down the road, who has good wheat every year. 

This year, I will stick with what I know: wheat and maize double-cropping on all 5 mu. I thought about cotton, but I am too old for all that spraying and hand-picking. My back cannot take it anymore. Wheat and maize can be harvested by machine, and my nephew helps me find a combine when the time comes.

For the winter wheat, I will rotary-till the land in early October, just like always. I will sow about 30 jin of improved wheat seed per mu — I save some seed from last year and buy a little to top up. For fertilizer, I will put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and then topdress with urea in the spring when the wheat starts jointing. I figure that is about 10 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I always worry about not having enough fertilizer, because a yellow wheat field means less food for my family. I will irrigate four times: once at planting, once before winter, once at green-up, and once at heading. The water costs money, but without it the wheat dries up. I will spray for weeds and bugs three or four times — the aphids come every year.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, there is no time to waste. I will plant summer maize right away, no-tillage, using hybrid seed I buy from the shop — one package per mu. The hybrid seed is more expensive, but it grows fast and strong. I will give the maize about 8 kg of nitrogen per mu, mostly as a base dressing, and some compound fertilizer. I will irrigate twice if the rain does not come, and spray for insects and weeds four or five times. The corn borers are bad some years.

I expect about 1,100 jin of wheat per mu and about 950 jin of maize per mu if the weather holds. Last year was decent, so I hope this year is the same. I do not have much cash, but I will borrow a little from my son in the city if I have to. Better to spend now than go hungry later.
